text:
Muscle lactate production increases when glycolysis produces pyruvate faster than the mitochondria can oxidize it. This happens in high-intensity exercise, in hypoxia, or when ATP demand is high. Lactate dehydrogenase then converts the excess pyruvate to lactate, which regenerates NAD⁺ so glycolysis can continue. The team note has this backwards: lactate is made *from* pyruvate, so blocking pyruvate formation would lower lactate production, not raise it.

CONFIDENCE: 85
